bullets: Moving materials around the body and the plant: the heart as a double pump, two blood loops, and the xylem and phloem highways
slides.heading: Transport: blood and the double circulation
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow blood around its two loops, meet the one artery that breaks the red rule, and see how plants move water and food without a heart.

bullets: Describe the heart as a double pump and trace the pulmonary and systemic loops
Name what xylem and phloem each carry, and correct the claim that every artery carries oxygen-rich blood
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: keep these in mind, because our exit ticket will ask you to trace both loops and to spot the exception artery.

bullets: Arteries are drawn red and carry blood away from the heart, so they feel like the oxygen pipe
But one artery leaves the heart carrying oxygen-poor blood - can a rule with an exception still be trusted?
slides.heading: The red artery that carries blue blood
slides.notes: Ask the class: if arteries always carry oxygenated blood, what colour should the artery to the lungs be? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the pulmonary artery breaks the rule.

bullets: An artery is defined by direction, not by oxygen: arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins carry it back
The heart is a double pump: the right side sends oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, the left side sends oxygen-rich blood to the body
Plants transport without a pump: xylem lifts water and minerals up, phloem moves food from the leaves
slides.heading: Direction defines the vessel
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the lesson: name vessels by where the blood is going, never by its colour. Every later scene is one journey on that map.

bullets: The left side pushes oxygen-rich blood out to the body while the right side pushes oxygen-poor blood to the lungs
Two pumps in one organ, beating together: that is why the heart can serve two loops at once
slides.heading: The heart is a double pump
slides.notes: Narrate each blood dot as it moves and ask the class to point at the side of the heart doing that job before you move on.

bullets: The pulmonary loop runs heart to lungs and back, loading oxygen; the systemic loop runs heart to body and back, delivering it
Blood passes through the heart twice on one full circuit: a double circulation
slides.heading: Two loops: heart to lungs, heart to body
slides.notes: Trace each loop with a finger as the animation draws it; the double pass through the heart is the point to land.

bullets: Xylem vessels carry water and minerals upward from the roots to the leaves
Phloem tubes move food made in the leaves to the parts that need it, up or down
slides.heading: Xylem lifts water; phloem shares food
slides.notes: Contrast the plant with the heart: no pump, yet water climbs and food travels. Ask which tube does which job before revealing.

bullets: The pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs, even though it is an artery
It is still an artery because it carries blood away from the heart: direction, not oxygen, makes an artery
slides.heading: A common mistake: arteries always carry oxygen
slides.notes: Name the trap plainly, then give the fix: judge the vessel by direction. The exit ticket returns to this exact exception.

bullets: Step 1: follow the pulmonary artery from the right side of the heart: it carries blood away from the heart, so it is an artery
Step 2: that blood is heading to the lungs to load oxygen, so it is oxygen-poor: the one artery that breaks the red rule
slides.heading: Worked example: testing the exception
slides.notes: Work this example slowly on the board; it is the exact reasoning the exit ticket asks for.

bullets: A circulation diagram is on your worksheet. Label the pulmonary loop and the systemic loop, and mark where blood loads and unloads oxygen
Careful - a classmate says the pulmonary artery must carry oxygen-rich blood because it is an artery. Explain, using direction, why that is wrong
slides.heading: Your turn: trace and explain
slides.notes: Give pairs four minutes; circulate and listen for the colour rule, because the script returns to it at the end.

bullets: On your own: name the exception artery and state what blood it carries and why it is still an artery
Watch out for the trap one last time: an artery is named by direction away from the heart, not by oxygen
slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
slides.notes: Collect the tickets at the door; they tell you who still uses the colour rule and who owns the direction rule.
